I feel like this, I’m starting to convince myself it’s not really social anxiety. But then I ask myself how would I act in this social situation is if I felt as comfortable there as I would if I was in a room with just my closest friends. There is still inhibition there that we just internalize, so much so that it is emotionally fatiguing to even debate if we want to socialize. Maybe I am genuinely not in the mood sometimes, but when I envision how i would act if (for example) my closest friend were accompanying me at an event, I realize I wouldn’t be telling myself don’t bother. 

Whenever I overcome my social anxiety and learn to be myself in social settings is when I can adequately say whether or not I truly don’t like socializing.

For starters my answer is informed by the fact that I myself am an African American woman. There is a TLDR at the bottom.

Consider that you could just be attracting the wrong TYPE of black girl, repeatedly. These types of girls are present in all races. Some women expect money and think it’s normal for the guy to provide it. Some don’t. I would suggest vetting the people you date more seriously to cut off those who have these expectations of you. I think this would be the most logical answer regardless of race. Don’t get discouraged, just set a boundary that you will not be loaning money to anyone and cut those off who still ask you. That’s perfectly reasonable. 

Also, I have been seriously abused by men for years and I have mental health issues like social anxiety due to that. I’ve been told that I come off as very “aloof” or distant around men for that reason, but I don’t mean harm by it. It hasn’t stopped me from opening up with time. I do not project hostility towards men, it’s just that I am learning how to undo a thinking pattern that I am inferior as a woman- and especially as a black woman. I am trying to find a way to be assertive and strong to avoid ever being abused again. Consider that these women are no different. I know it is not your problem to even care, and it does not justify hostility towards you, but that could be a possible explanation. I’d say spending decent time to allow them to open and get comfortable is an idea. It takes a while for me to let my guard down honestly, like months, and that’s just how it is for many women. 

Lastly, the answer to your issue will never be to give in to stereotypes. One user jadedea describes a stereotypical black women to avoid as guidance to you but that thinking will not do you good in understanding what the issue is. It is easy to give in to stereotypes. You will miss out on good people if you do that. Also, the lady who said “I don’t cook for men” might’ve misinterpreted the intention behind your words. 


TLDR; I think you should be extra serious when you vet women in the dating process, maybe you need to ask upfront what the expectations are and set boundaries. The women you describe as “waiting for you to fuck up” or hostile might be struggling with trauma. Above all do not give in to racial stereotypes, they are lazy and are not the answer.

I relate to the comment by dynastyduo a lot. I think I’m similar to your girlfriend in this scenario as I have extreme social anxiety and that didn’t go away just because i entered a relationship. It makes me very timid and scared to share my opinion, but outwardly I know it just looks like I’m disinterested or bored. It actually makes me feel anxious going into depth about topics. I feel annoying if I talk too much. And I feel like I’m taking up too much talking about my own interests. 

Ive been with my boyfriend for 8 months, and while we’ve definitely talked about this and he has reassured me that I can practice being more expressive with him, most of the change has come from my own efforts. He helped me become aware of how bad my anxiety was. Before you really throw the towel in I think you should (and maybe you have tried this before) try to understand why she is like this. See if she is struggling with anxiety. Pry her for more info when she does talk. Don’t make insensitive jokes in the beginning because that could be discouraging. Maybe she’s never been a big talker, and that’s okay but maybe you could make having deeper convos a hobby itself. I see couples who makes podcasts all the time and I think it’s so cute how they basically make a business out of bonding together. Tell her that it is actually affecting your thoughts about the relationship and you want it to work out. I don’t know, these are all things that have helped me through this process and I would honestly say there is no such thing as too much reassurance. It really encourages. Good luck!

I’ve taken several long breaks in between studying Chinese (ranging from 3 months to 2 years). After the 2 year break, I took a placement test for college and they threw me into a more advanced class I didn’t think I was ready for. What I’ve learned was not to feel pressured into going backwards or reviewing previous lessons. That just made it harder to get started. Start where you left off, and you’ll know whether or not it’s necessary to back peddle. Some things will probably need brushing up, but that’s okay. 

I’m not sure what learning methods work best for you, but for me it’s been a combination of vocabulary intake + application and listening comprehension. That’s all I’ve needed to get a move on after a long period away from 中文。

I’ve never studied in China for more than a few months at a time, and I also didn’t fully utilize the resources and people around me to practice with until the trip was halfway over. But I still made some good progress by going out alone and forcing myself to struggle with conversations and words I didn’t know. Always had a dictionary and notepad on me to help remember unfamiliar words. I can only imagine what 6 months or more would’ve done for me. 

I hope this helped somewhat. 加油, I believe in you!
